### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeSourceSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `124c275a339603027b7130f1986eb75275f4643d` — the merge of head `4f6792529c3a86ae2e44e249fa4c8bada27956fe` into base `4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 124c275a339603027b7130f1986eb75275f4643d && git checkout 124c275a339603027b7130f1986eb75275f4643d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49 4f6792529c3a86ae2e44e249fa4c8bada27956fe && git checkout -B drift-repro 4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49 && git merge --no-ff 4f6792529c3a86ae2e44e249fa4c8bada27956fe

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4f6792529c3a86ae2e44e249fa4c8bada27956fe`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/knowledge-source.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.knowledge-source-registration-governed.ts, docs/adr/0084-application-builder-information-architecture.md + packages/spec/src/ai/knowledge-source.test.ts
Security-touching: yes

Inputs read: card #37740 (body, triage, claim, dev report) and folded card #37741 (body, triage, claim); PR #38015 body and file list; the net diff against `main` (6 files, 98 insertions, 18 deletions); the 70 check-runs on this head. Remainder of the diff, left to the lane seat: `.changeset/37741-knowledge-source-code-door-prescription.md` (read for ② only) and the generated `content/docs/references/ai/knowledge-source.mdx`.

Check-runs on the head: 70, all completed; 0 failed; 60 success, 10 skipped (the opt-in and placeholder rows: Lint UI, Temporal Conformance, the Dogfood matrix placeholder, Dogfood Verify CLI, UI Published Artifacts, Borrowed queue verdict, Queue verdict, 18.x upgrade harness, Packed-tarball smoke, Schedule gate). Test Core 1 to 10, Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Lint (ESLint, docs and code guards, repo and tooling gates, CI release and engine gates, PM dispatch-gates), Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, Build Docs, Check Documentation Links and Governed Surface Queue Guard are all success. The one family the dev left to CI (the CLI spawn test `migrate-meta-engine-guidance.test.ts`) sits in Test Core, which is green.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set of `KnowledgeSourceSchema`, `ObjectKnowledgeSourceSchema`, `KnowledgeRefreshPolicySchema`: unchanged. Every hunk in `knowledge-source.zod.ts` is a string term (`+ CODE_DOOR_18`) inside an existing `retiredKey(...)` message or the existing `'*'` regex message. Nothing that parsed is refused and nothing refused now parses. Right.
- Public surface: `CODE_DOOR_18` is a module-private const (no `export`), so no export is added; the api-surface and authorable-surface gates ran green in CI. What is published and does change is text: seven refusal messages (six tombstones and the `'*'` member), the generated reference page that copies them, and three fields of the semantic entry `knowledge-source-registration-governed` (`replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`) that `os migrate meta --from 18` prints. Right, and declared as such.
- Count of uses, read at the head: `CODE_DOOR_18` occurs 8 times in the file (1 definition, 7 uses); the 7 uses are `refresh.cron`, `source.contentFields`, the `'*'` member, `id`, `adapterConfig`, `embedding`, `vectorStore`. Each stands directly before the migrate sentence (`MIGRATE_18` six times, the `'*'` member's own sentence once), which stays last. The `file` / `http` prescription is untouched and names no command to run. Right.
- Migration chain: no conversion, no `conversionIds`, no `relevantWhen` is added or changed; the entry keeps `conversionIds: ['knowledge-source-id-to-name']` and carries no `relevantWhen`, so it is printed on every `--from 18` run that crosses hop 19, whatever the stack holds. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.
- ADR-0084: no table row, no Order or Tier cell, no Status line and no heading anchor changes; `studioMenuPlacement.ts` at the head already lists `ai_context` then `knowledge_source`, both `advanced` (lines 121 and 122), and its test is in the green UI shards. Right.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/37741-knowledge-source-code-door-prescription.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Matches the diff: message text and upgrade-entry text only, no shape, no accept-set move, no narrowing. The ADR-0084 edits publish nothing and need no bump. The Check Changeset run is green.

Clause-②: no. Agreed: no authorable capability is taken away or added at any consumer.

### ③ Boundary flags

Open question (item 6's closing note, the clause "its schema requires one object ... so the first test of the rule sorts it 高级"): **A is the true one; keep the clause.**
- Against the ADR text. The rule's first test reads "It has no parent object. Its schema does not require one object." and the section ends "The rule sorts the next type; the table records what was ruled." Applying test 1 to a type registered after the ruling is therefore what the record itself prescribes, and item 6 already does exactly that for `ai_context`. The note says "the same three sentences place it"; the three are the first test, "高级 holds every type the ruling does not list as 常用" and "a type with no row is drawn at the end of its group". Option B would leave two sentences under a lead-in that says three, so B is not a one-clause strike without a second edit.
- Against the code. `KnowledgeSourceSchema.source` is required and is `ObjectKnowledgeSourceSchema`; its `object` key is a required `z.string()`; `kind` has one live value, `object` (`file` and `http` are retired values). So every `knowledge_source` names exactly one object. The clause is a checkable fact and the parenthesis says honestly where the key sits (inside `source`, not at the root as for `ai_context`).
- It places nothing: the row, its order and its tier were written by PR #37676 and are mirrored in `studioMenuPlacement.ts`; the two sentences that follow place the type without it. No escalation needed.

Dev premise corrections, each checked:
- "35 entries, 34 rows, AI 5" at `origin/main` `62dd9e1ef5`: confirmed. `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` at that commit (and byte-identical at the head) holds 35 entries: data 8, ui 7, automation 2, system 7, security 6, ai 5. The enum `MetadataTypeSchema` also holds 35. The table at the head has 34 rows: Data 8, UI 6, Automation 2, Platform 7, Access 6, AI 5; the one entry without a row is `form` (`ui`). The card's "33" was stale. `form` entered the registry on 2026-11-27 (PR #37366, which fixes #37086) and `knowledge_source` on 2026-11-27 (PR #37676), as the note says.
- "The ADR-0087 D3 entry is the registry entry file, not text in ADR-0087": confirmed, `docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md` holds no line mentioning knowledge. ADR-0087 is rightly untouched.

Dev deviations:
- Fifth place in ADR-0084 (the count pointer in the sentence that introduces the table): accepted; leaving it would contradict the note it points at. See N3 for its form.
- Entry file in place of `docs/adr/0087`, the regenerated reference page, the changeset: accepted, all three follow from the card.
- Two wording commits on the entry ("on an adapter that embeds"; the list of what starts the build removed): both make the text truer; accepted.
- Footer, tier-line and trailer deviations are process matters for the seat, not contract.

Out-of-scope notes from the dev: (a) `.changeset/37304-knowledge-source-governed-type.md` and `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx` say the index is found again with no underscore exception. Outside this review's scope and true for every id that is a legal name; a follow-up card is the right carrier and the dev filed none, so the seat should place one or accept it by name. (b) "`field` carries no order and no tier because it draws no row" does not mention `datasource`: still true as written, a lag in a neighbour's sentence, not this card's.

Security-touching is `yes` on a conservative reading of one sentence only: the entry's `reason` now says that the renamed source's content fields "are sent to the embedding provider again", which is a statement about data leaving the deployment. No changed hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour, and the sentence restates what a first build already does for the same fields and the same provider. The seat may read that as not security-teaching; nothing else in the diff comes near.

SQL push-down: the diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ai/knowledge-source.zod.ts` (against card #37741 and the code it cites)
- The code door named in the seven prescriptions exists in both spellings: `KnowledgeServicePluginOptions.sources` (`knowledge-service-plugin.ts:331`, registered at boot at `:568`) and `registerSource` (`IKnowledgeService`, `contracts/knowledge-service.ts:178`; `KnowledgeService.registerSource`, `knowledge-service.ts:271`). The service's own refusal text uses the same two spellings (`knowledge-source-registry.ts` `DOOR_TEXT.code`).
- "is in no stack collection, so `os migrate meta` lists no edit for it": true. The three 19 conversions (`knowledge-source-id-to-name`, `knowledge-source-content-fields-to-content`, `knowledge-source-inert-keys-removed`) all walk `mapCollection(stack, 'knowledgeSources', ...)` and nothing else; a plugin option or a `registerSource` call is never visited.
- The jsdoc's "every source written against 18 is such a registration": true. At tag `@objectstack/spec@18.6.0` the stack schema has no `knowledgeSources` key (the 18 source file itself says `defineStack({ knowledgeSources })` is refused); the key first exists in `stack.zod.ts` on 19.
- What the migrate sentence promises is what the command does for a stack that holds sources: `id` to `name` and `contentFields` to `content` are renames, `embedding`, `vectorStore`, `adapterConfig` and `refresh.cron` are lossless deletes, and a `'*'` member is kept and reported as a TODO, which is what the `'*'` message's own sentence says. `--from` and `--write` are real flags of `os migrate meta`.
- Break attempts that did not break it: a mixed app (sources in the stack and in code) reads both sentences correctly; the `file` / `http` prescription correctly stays without the sentence; the test pins position (each of the three phrases before the command sentence) and the dev's ablation shows the pin goes red for one tombstone.

`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.knowledge-source-registration-governed.ts` (sentence by sentence against the live code)
- "A `name` starts with a letter" / "an id could start with an underscore": the 18 pattern was `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$`, `ROUTER_ADDRESSABLE_NAME_PATTERN` is `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`. The leading underscore is the only spelling newly refused, so "one source is the exception" is exact, not a sample.
- "an adapter keys everything it holds for a source by the source's name": true in all three adapters at the head (`ctx.source.name` in memory, pgvector, turso) and in the contract (`AdapterContext.source.name` is the index key). In 18 the same adapters keyed by `ctx.source.id`, so the old key is the old id.
- "built from nothing under its new name": true, the new key has no generation in any adapter.
- "the service drops the index of a `knowledge_source` item it stops serving and never that of a registration in code": true. `dropMetadataSource` returns early unless `entry.door === 'metadata'`, its one caller is the metadata loader, and `unregisterSource` only forgets the entry ("The index it built stays with its adapter"). No other code in the service, the CLI or the runtime calls `dropSource`.
- "nothing searches that index or keeps it in step with the records": true; search, event sync, the reap guard and the scheduled reconcile all walk registered sources.
- "call `dropSource({ source })` on that adapter (`IKnowledgeService.getAdapter`), where `source` is the source with its `name` set to the old id": works on every adapter in the tree. `getAdapter` is on the contract (`:173`); `dropSource` takes an `AdapterContext` whose only required member is `source`; memory deletes the key, pgvector retires and sweeps by `source_id`, and turso's `SAFE_SOURCE_ID` (`^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$`) admits the underscore-led id and also drops the legacy table of the cloud-repo releases. The contract says a drop for a source the adapter holds nothing for is not an error, so an unneeded call is harmless.
- "An adapter without `dropSource` keeps that index until it is removed in the adapter's own store": matches the contract (the member is optional).
- The acceptance criterion added for the underscore case is checkable through `indexStatus` and does not contradict the general one before it.
- Card acceptance ("states the underscore-led id's stale index and how it is dropped"): met.

`docs/adr/0084-application-builder-information-architecture.md` (against the registry, the table and its first consumer)
- All five edits read true for the table as merged (counts in ③). The fold sentence's note agrees with "A 高级 type is drawn by the area's existing rule, when the package holds one". The amendment-table row's note and item 6's heading and closing note agree with the two table rows that point at item 6. Struck text is kept, each note is dated and names its card, and each says it decides nothing; that is the record's own form (compare the notes of cards #37564 and #37920 beside it). ADR link, anchor and symbol-anchor gates are green in CI.
- Card #37740 acceptance: met; `studioMenuPlacement.test.ts` is in the green UI shards.

`packages/spec/src/ai/knowledge-source.test.ts` (implementing file): the pin agrees with the contract, sentence by sentence: both spellings of the door and "in the registration itself", each before the command sentence, on the six tombstone rows and the `'*'` row; the existing `endsWith(MIGRATE)` pin still holds the house rule.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

N1 — The entry says without condition "The adapter also keeps the index it built under the old id". Of the adapters in the tree, only `knowledge-memory` was published in 18 (the pgvector and turso packages start at 19.0.0-next.0), and its store is process memory, which the restart of an upgrade empties. The sentence holds for a persistent store (a custom adapter, the turso tables of the cloud-repo releases, a pgvector index built on a 19 prerelease). The prescribed call is a harmless no-op where nothing is held, so nothing is wrong in effect; a half-clause ("where its store outlives the process") would make it exact. Prose in a spec file: leave as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card.
N2 — The code-door sentence tells the author of a registration that `os migrate meta` "lists no edit for it", while the only place the underscore case and its `dropSource` instruction are printed is that command's manual notices (this entry has no `relevantWhen`, so it prints for such an app too). The `id` tombstone beside it still says, without condition, "the value is unchanged, so the source's index is found again and is not rebuilt". An author with an underscore-led id therefore meets the tombstone, then the name grammar's refusal, and is pointed at the stale index only if they run the command anyway. The card placed the exception in the entry, not the tombstone, so this is as ruled; a follow-up could add "its manual notices still apply" to the sentence.
N3 — The fifth place (the pointer in the sentence that introduces the table) is edited in place, with no date and no card on it, where the other four are dated notes. It is a pointer and the note it points at carries the date and the card, so the reader loses nothing; noted because the record's form elsewhere is add-only.
N4 — An 18 id of the exact shape `_p` + 16 hex characters + `_` + a name would equal the index key the service spells for a package's source, and a drop under that old id would then name a live index. Not reachable in practice (a 64-bit match on a hand-written id); recorded only because the entry tells the author to pass the old id verbatim.

**Shape and gates.** 6 files, +98/-18. Check-runs at 4f679252: 60 success, 10 expected skip, 0 failed. Governed (`docs/adr/**`), plus the published schema text in `knowledge-source.zod.ts` and the migration entry. `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none`. `l1-face` flags one item, `keywords-other-cards`, for `Fixes #37741`. **The parts left to me.**

- **`content/docs/references/ai/knowledge-source.mdx`.** Regenerated output. The eight rows changed (`cron` and `contentFields` appear twice) carry the code-door sentence in the same place as the source messages.

**Open question (1): A, keep the clause.** The record rules it in ③. Item 6's lead-in says three sentences place the type, so dropping the clause would leave two and is not a one-clause edit. The clause restates the first test, which the schema's required `object` key meets. **(2)** The 35-entry count is confirmed at both 62dd9e1ef5 and the head. **(3)** The spawn test the dev left to CI runs in Test Core, which is green.

**Security-touching.** The record says `yes`, conservatively, for one sentence: a renamed source's content fields are sent to the embedding provider again. No hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential or authentication behaviour. The seat adopting the record decides on the label.

**Follow-up for the seat.** The dev's out-of-scope note has no carrier card: `.changeset/37304-knowledge-source-governed-type.md` and `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx` do not mention the underscore exception. File one small card, or accept it by name. Record nits N1 to N4 are accepted as they stand.

**Landing:** governed, so it goes through the seat's Tier H handoff, not area label-write --land.
